claims.assertion: Kubernetes multi-tenancy can use namespace-per-tenant or virtual control planes within a shared cluster, while dedicated clusters provide a separate control-plane lifecycle at higher overhead.
claims.anchor: Isolation; Implementations; Namespace per tenant; Virtual control plane per tenant
claims.scope: Current official documentation checked 2026-09-19; topology does not select or certify the platform threat model.

claims.assertion: The Kubernetes Multi-Tenancy Working Group taxonomy distinguishes Namespaces as a Service, Clusters as a Service and Control Planes as a Service.
claims.anchor: Namespaces as a Service; Clusters as a Service; Control planes as a Service
claims.scope: 2021 architectural taxonomy checked against current multi-tenancy documentation on 2026-09-19; dated project details and survey figures are not reused.

claims.assertion: A Kubernetes ServiceAccount is a namespaced non-human cluster identity, while least-privilege API permissions are granted separately through RBAC roles and bindings.
claims.anchor: What are service accounts?; Use cases for Kubernetes service accounts
claims.scope: Current official documentation checked 2026-09-19; ServiceAccount identity is not treated as end-user identity, MCP authorization or approval.

claims.assertion: Pods are non-isolated by default per traffic direction, and a NetworkPolicy has no effect unless the cluster network plugin implements its enforcement.
claims.anchor: Prerequisites; The two sorts of pod isolation; What you can't do with network policies
claims.scope: Current L3/L4 NetworkPolicy semantics checked 2026-09-19; no claim is made about this repository having a CNI or live policy enforcement.

claims.assertion: ResourceQuota limits aggregate namespace consumption, requests inform scheduling, and Linux resource limits are passed to the runtime and enforced through kernel cgroups with resource-specific behavior.
claims.anchor: Requests and limits; How Pods with resource requests are scheduled; How Kubernetes applies resource requests and limits
claims.scope: Current official documentation plus the ResourceQuota concept page checked 2026-09-19; resource governance is not presented as confidentiality or an application token budget.

claims.assertion: seccomp restricts syscalls and RuntimeDefault uses a runtime-provided profile, while privileged mode can override key kernel hardening and stronger sandboxing carries additional resource/compatibility cost.
claims.anchor: seccomp; Considerations for seccomp; Kernel-level security features and privileged containers
claims.scope: Current official concept page and seccomp tutorial checked 2026-09-19; no hard-isolation guarantee for an unspecified cluster is inferred.

findings.location: Как наш локальный baseline отображается на Kubernetes
findings.rationale: The first draft implied that moving a Bubblewrap runner to an ordinary Pod necessarily weakens the kernel boundary, although both normally rely on the host kernel.
findings.resolution: Replaced the comparison with the narrower claim that a Pod does not automatically strengthen the kernel boundary and that mount/network/resource restrictions must be reimplemented and verified; reread.

findings.rationale: A generic statement that every resource overrun is rejected hid different CPU and memory limit behavior, and 'private network namespace' could be confused with a configured private network.
findings.resolution: Changed the expected test result to the declared bounded outcome and described the local runner as a separate network namespace without configured egress; reread.
